## The hotspot set

Pulling the three requested slices out of the 87 findings:

**`high_fan_in_fan_out` (all 8, confidence 0.7):**

| File | Fan-in | Fan-out | Cutoffs | Finding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | **18** | 1 | p95 9 / p99 10 | crime_00044 |
| `src/plugin.ts` | **10** | 3 | p95 9 / p99 10 | crime_00013 |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 | 0 | p95 9 | crime_00031 |
| `test/utils.ts` | 9 | 0 | p95 9 | crime_00087 |
| `src/index.ts` | 4 | **17** | p95 6 / p99 11 | crime_00070 |
| `src/esbuild/index.ts` | 1 | **11** | p99 11 | crime_00039 |
| `src/rollup.ts` | 0 | 7 | p95 6 | crime_00068 |
| `src/api-extractor.ts` | 1 | 6 | p95 6 | crime_00050 |

**`large_file`:** `docs/README.md` 679 lines (2.3×, high), `src/index.ts` 460 (1.5×), `src/utils.ts` 425 (1.4×).

**Top `large_function`:** `src/index.ts` `build` 293 lines (4.9×), `src/index.ts` `<anonymous>` 274, `src/esbuild/index.ts` `runEsbuild` 237, `src/index.ts` `mainTasks` 194, `src/cli-main.ts` `main` 153, `src/esbuild/postcss.ts` `postcssPlugin` 140.

The detector name bundles two opposite risks, and the triage hinges on separating them: **fan-in is blast radius** (my edits break other people), **fan-out is fragility** (other people's edits break me). Only fan-in reduction answers the question as asked; fan-out tells you how *cheap* a refactor is.

## Triage order

### 1. `src/utils.ts` — refactor first
Fan-in **18**, double the p95 cutoff of 9 and the highest in a 52-file repo; the score puts 29 files in its transitive blast radius. It's also 425 lines (crime_00046) with 7 sync I/O calls spread across three unrelated functions — `removeFiles`, `ensureTempDeclarationDir`, and more (crime_00004). That combination is the actual pathology: 18 modules import a 425-line grab drawer, so *every* edit to it nominally touches all 18, regardless of which concern you changed.

Notably there is **no** `large_function` finding here — this is a breadth problem, not a God-function problem. Split by responsibility (fs ops / path handling / formatting) behind a re-export barrel so the 18 importers keep working, then let them narrow their imports over time. That's the single largest reduction in codebase-wide blast radius available.

### 2. `src/index.ts` — refactor second, and it's the cheapest big win
Fan-out **17** against a p99 cutoff of 11 — the most coupled file in the repo — but fan-in only **4**. It carries 460 lines (crime_00069) and six of the largest functions in the scan: `build` at 293 lines (4.9× threshold), an anonymous 274-liner nested inside it, `mainTasks` 194, `normalizeOptions` 96, `startWatcher` 79, `buildAll` 75. Plus `build` is a `name_behavior_mismatch` (crime_00032) — a "pure-sounding" name calling `createLogger` and `removeFiles`.

Fan-in 4 is what makes this the best risk/reward on the list: it holds the most mass and the fewest downstream consumers, so extraction is nearly ripple-free. It doesn't reduce anyone else's blast radius, but it's where the agent-confusion surface actually lives.

### 3. `src/plugin.ts` — high value, surgical only
Fan-in **10** (at the p99 cutoff), fan-out 3, `buildFinished` at 103 lines (crime_00003), and the highest `agent_risk` of any connectivity finding at 0.44. The reason it ranks below utils.ts despite similar load-bearing status: `test_gap` 0.5 — there's no test signal protecting it, whereas utils.ts scores 0. Extract helpers *inside* `buildFinished`; do not move the module's exported surface. Ten importers is not a boundary you renegotiate without tests.

### 4. `src/esbuild/index.ts` — safe cleanup, do it whenever
Fan-out **11** (exactly p99) but fan-in **1**. `runEsbuild` is 237 lines (4.0× threshold, crime_00002) and takes an options bag with **38 distinct property reads** (crime_00015). High local agent risk, essentially zero blast radius — one importer. Worth doing, but it buys you nothing codebase-wide, so it doesn't compete for first position.

## Leave alone

**`src/log.ts` — the most important "don't touch."** Fan-in 9, fan-out **0**, and the *highest* transitive blast radius in the repo at 30 importers. But its only findings are two unprefixed booleans (`onlyImportant`, `silent` — crime_00030, severity 0.3, effort "quick"). A leaf logger with zero fan-out and high fan-in is correct architecture, not a crime; the detector's own fix shape ("split or invert: too many consumers means too much coupling") is wrong for this file. Renaming a boolean here ripples across 30 files to buy a naming convention. Suppress it.

**`docs/README.md`** — the highest-severity `large_file` in the scan (0.85, 679 lines) and completely irrelevant to blast radius: 0 importers, it's Markdown. It ranks high only because `large_file` scores on line count without a code/prose distinction. The one reason to touch it is unrelated — crime_00016 flags no `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` anywhere in the repo, so carving agent-facing docs out of that 679-liner has value as *context* work, not refactoring.

**`src/rollup.ts`** — fan-out 7, fan-in **0**, `blast_radius` literally 0. `getRollupConfig` is 122 lines with a name/behaviour mismatch (calls `setSilent`, `removeFiles`). Real problems, zero ripple. Opportunistic only.

**`src/api-extractor.ts`** — fan-out 6 against a p95 cutoff of exactly 6, fan-in 1. It qualified for "top connectivity tier" by a margin of zero on a 52-file sample. Treat as noise.

**`test/utils.ts`** (fan-in 9, test scaffolding) and **`src/cli-main.ts`** (`main` 153 lines, but fan-in 2 and no connectivity finding — entry points are supposed to be wide).

## Two caveats on the evidence

**`churn` and `recency` are 0 on all 87 findings.** There's no git history signal in this scan, so the ranking is purely structural. Real churn data would likely reorder tiers 2–4 — a 237-line function nobody has edited in a year is a different problem than one touched weekly.

**The `test_gap: 0` scores are softer than they look.** `src/utils.ts` and `src/index.ts` both score 0 (tests exist), which is part of why I put them first. But the scan also flags 12 tests with **zero** assertions (crime_00052–63) and 14 more with only weak matchers, several in `test/index.test.ts` itself. The safety net under tiers 1 and 2 is thinner than the score implies — worth pinning behaviour with real assertions on the code paths you're about to move before you move them.
